rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template: it was issued one day earlier and uses the same sequence of recitals and operative machinery—lands previously reserved for military purposes, a finding that specified parcels are no longer needed, a public-interest determination, restoration or transfer to a nonfederal governmental body, and a detailed metes-and-bounds description. C04 and C24 are close structural precedents, but C23 is the strongest because of its immediate temporal proximity and especially close sequence and phrasing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: certain lands ... were acquired ... by the War Department for use as a military reservation ... [and] being no longer needed for military purposes
shared_material.parent_excerpt: certain lands ... were reserved for military purposes ... [and] certain parcels of such lands are no longer needed for military purposes
shared_material.explanation: Both begin with the lands' military-reservation history and then establish that particular parcels are surplus to military needs.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Whereas it appears that such a transfer would be in the public interest; Now, Therefore ... do hereby grant and transfer
shared_material.parent_excerpt: it is deemed advisable and in the public interest that they be restored ... NOW THEREFOR, The possession, use, and control ... are hereby restored
shared_material.explanation: The public-interest recital directly leads to an operative governmental transfer of the identified land.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the said Lot 14 ... excepting and reserving therefrom the following-described tract of land ... From corner No. 7 ...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The possession, use, and control of the following-described parcels ... are hereby restored ... Beginning at concrete monument No. 7 ...
shared_material.explanation: Each operative provision identifies surveyed parcels and incorporates detailed boundary descriptions, reflecting substantially parallel land-disposition machinery.
